topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the core learning outcomes concerning cancer etiology and carcinogen assessment.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, contrasting intrinsic random mutation processes with environmental exposures and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Agents, Promoters, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the specific biological, chemical, and physical mechanisms through which pathogens, environmental mutagens, metabolic activation, chronic inflammation, and tumour promotion drive malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogens and establish causal links to cancer.

topics.label: Carcinogen Risk Assessment and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing summary on the difficulty of assessing carcinogen potency and the practical balance between environmental risk and benefit.
